findings.body:
**Preserve exit 3 for `needs-human` results.**

At `src/queue-runner/runner.ts:177`, a `LiveDispatch` result with `status: 'needs-human'` and no explicit `exitCode` receives exit 1. Map this status to exit 3 before applying the generic failure fallback.

As per coding guidelines, “Exit codes: 0 clean, 1 thrown error, 2 arg error, 3 needs-human.” Based on learnings, defer this Minor correction to a follow-up issue.
findings.title: Preserve exit 3 for `needs-human` results.

findings.body:
**Derive the repository and state root from one `config.json` read in `reconcile-merged`.**

The `reconcile-merged` branch reads `repo` from `config.json` at `src/queue-runner/crq.ts:141`. It then calls `publisherStateRoot(root)` at line 153, which reads `config.json` again. If the file changes between these awaited reads, the unit can receive repository A with a state root derived from the changed configuration. The reconcile effects then load and write `queue.json`, the tick lock, and the reconcile wrappers under that state root, and enroll work for the first repository. The inspected path has no check that the state root belongs to `repo`. The binding check at `src/ops/crq/reconcileMerged.ts:173` refuses only stored wrappers that record a different repository. It does not validate `queue.json`.

The second read also falls back silently. If `config.json` becomes unreadable between the two reads, `publisherStateRoot` returns `<runner>/state` (`crq.ts:282`) instead of failing.

Read `repo` and `state_root` from a single parsed configuration object, and return a failure when that object is unusable.
findings.title: Derive the repository and state root from one `config.json` read in `reconcile-merged`.
Keep the scanned range in profile-launched review commands.

findings.body:
**Decode Git-quoted diff paths before the denylist path match.**

Git quotes unified-diff path headers that contain unusual characters. A tab, quote, backslash, or non-ASCII byte in a filename triggers quoting. For a file named `src/` followed by a tab and `probe.txt`, the `+++` header carries the quoted form `"b/src/\tprobe.txt"`. Line 85 strips `b/` only when the value starts with `b/`. The quoted value starts with `"`, so the prefix is kept, along with the quotes and the `\t` escape. Line 92 stores that value as `path`. The matcher then tests path-scoped rules against it at `src/adapters/crq/reviewRegexWorker.ts:14`. A rule such as `path: '^src/'` does not match the encoded string, so its lines can go unmatched. The same encoded path also reaches the allow-list test at line 91.

Decode the quoted value before the prefix strip at line 85. Unescape `\\`, `\"`, `\t`, `\n`, and octal byte sequences, and decode the bytes as UTF-8. Apply the same decoding to the `diff --git` path at line 73. Add a test that a path-scoped rule matches a file whose name needs quoting.
findings.title: Decode Git-quoted diff paths before the denylist path match.

findings.body:
**Give open and delta spawn failures a terminal state.**

When spawning an `open` or `delta` review fails with `ReviewSpawnError`, the item stays reserved. `reserveAndSpawnReview` saves `state: 'reviewing'`, `run.pid: null`, and `launch_pending: true` before spawning (`src/queue-runner/reviewLaunch.ts:109`). The catch block rethrows the error for these kinds (`src/queue-runner/reviewLaunch.ts:114-115`), so the failed-state transition at lines 117-141 does not run. No `exit.json` is written on this path. The tick then classifies the run as `ambiguous` and never harvests it (`src/queue-runner/tick.ts:348-355`). The reservation stays in the held set and keeps counting against admission slots (`src/policy/crq/tickAdmission.ts:90-100`). No code in `src/` clears it. Repeated failures can exhaust `max_inflight` and block other reviews.

Route `open` and `delta` through the same terminal spawn-failure transition used for `author` and `local-review` (`failed` state, `spawn_failed_at`, `last_error`), keeping the no-retry behavior. Confirm that the `failed` state is handled for these kinds before merging.
findings.title: Give open and delta spawn failures a terminal state.

findings.body:
**Exclude fork PRs from parent-candidate matching.**

`chain` selects a parent PR by `headRef` alone. The listing adapter does not provide head-repository identity. It requests `number,isDraft,baseRefName,headRefName,headRefOid` and maps `headRef: row.headRefName`, so a fork PR can match a primary PR's `base` and become that PR's only parent candidate. If the fork PR targets a configured branch, `chain` returns true. The primary PR is then treated as stacked on a parent that does not exist in the base repository.

Add the cross-repository flag to `OpenPr` and the `gh pr list` field set, then skip cross-repository rows when selecting parents:

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-    const parents = opened.filter((candidate) => candidate.headRef === current?.base);
+    const parents = opened.filter(
+      (candidate) => !candidate.crossRepository && candidate.headRef === current?.base,
+    );
```

</details>

The adapter must populate `crossRepository` from `isCrossRepository` in `src/adapters/crq/openPrDiscoverySource.ts`. Same-repository parents keep their current behavior.
findings.title: Exclude fork PRs from parent-candidate matching.

findings.body:
**Skip repair suppression when the PR base changed.**

At `src/queue-runner/openPrDiscovery.ts:198`, `ownRange(queue, previous, pr.head)` returns true for the head range only. The call does not pass the current `pin` base, and the `ownRange` contract (line 36) takes no base argument. If the PR was retargeted from `B1` to an older allowed base `B0`, and the new head `H2` contains only owned repairs after the prior head `H1`, this `continue` skips enrollment. The `B0..B1` range that the retarget added to the PR is never reviewed. The equivalence check at line 204 would have rejected this range because its captured `base` differs, but the earlier `continue` prevents it from running.

Apply the repair suppression only when captured evidence for `previous` used the current `pin` as its base. Otherwise, continue to the equivalence check and enroll the full-range delta.
findings.title: Skip repair suppression when the PR base changed.
Stop coalescing pending ranges into an existing terminal item ID.
